item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Macron Faults Trump For Shifting U.S. Goals
item.summary: The French president said President Trump could not be taken seriously because he had repeatedly changed his goals for the Iran war. He also criticized the president for berating NATO.

item.title: U.K. to Host Talks on Securing Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: It was not clear whether the talks, expected to involve dozens of countries, would satisfy President Trump’s demand that other nations take a more active part in the Iran war.

item.title: Evacuated From War-Torn Gaza, 11 Toddlers Return Home to Hugs and Tears
item.summary: The Palestinian children were born prematurely in the early days of the war and moved from a besieged hospital to Egypt. They have now returned home to the enclave, which lies in ruins.

item.title: Lost Friendships, Broken Relationships: How the War in Iran Is Dividing the Diaspora
item.summary: Amid months of protest, repression and war in their native country, Iranians living abroad are navigating their biggest rifts yet.

item.title: Macron Snaps Back at Trump’s Mockery and Criticism of NATO
item.summary: President Emmanuel Macron of France suggested that President Trump’s daily comments on the war in Iran were unserious. “Maybe one shouldn’t speak every day,” Mr. Macron told reporters.

item.title: Iranian officials come out defiant after Trump’s war speech.
In a Muzzled Russia, He Still Speaks His Mind
item.summary: While hundreds of other journalists fled into exile after Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dmitri A. Muratov stayed. But he did not stay quiet.

item.title: In UK Prisons, Drones Fly In Contraband ‘As if by Uber Eats’
item.summary: Decades-old prison buildings were designed to be secure from the ground but not the air. Experts say that makes a lucrative smuggling trade hard to tackle.

item.title: Danish Warship Sunk by Britain’s Lord Nelson 225 Years Ago Is Found
item.summary: The ship sank during the Battle of Copenhagen, an important moment in Danish and British history, and became the origin of a common saying.

item.title: After Sting Operation, Cousin of Bashar al-Assad Convicted in Arms for Drugs Deal
item.summary: The cousin, Antoine Kassis, was found guilty of conspiracy to support a terrorist group, after trying to sell weapons from the fallen regime to a Colombian militia.
